children: While Egypt maintains a diversified external funding strategy that includes sukuk and sustainable bonds, the country is also accelerating efforts to lengthen the maturity profile of its domestic debt and increase local-currency borrowing, S&P Global Ratings told Zawya.
The ratings agency said the government is prioritising domestic debt issuance to increase the share of local-currency borrowing in its debt portfolio and reduce refinancing risk.
A key objective is extending maturities from the current weighted average of about 1.5 years through greater issuance of longer-dated local bonds.
S&P also expects Egypt to continue issuing sukuk after its debut domestic sovereign sukuk sale in November 2025 broadened its investor base by attracting Shariah-compliant investors.

On the external side, the government is expected to maintain a diversified funding approach, with a focus on concessional and semi-concessional financing. Potential funding tools include eurobonds, green and sustainable bonds, as well as guaranteed issues such as Panda and Samurai bonds.

S&P credits Egypt with having built a strong position in sustainable finance by leading several sovereign green financing initiatives in the MENA region. The agency said the finance ministry’s sustainable finance framework could support future green, social or sustainability bond issuance when market conditions are favourable.

Egypt became the first sovereign in the Middle East and North Africa to issue a green bond, raising $750 million in 2020. It followed that with Africa's first sovereign sustainable Panda bond worth RMB 3.5 billion in 2023 and, most recently, an 80 billion yen ($500 million) sustainability Samurai bond in June 2026.
The ratings agency noted that Egypt’s financial markets remain sensitive to swings in global risk appetite because of the participation of foreign investors in local government debt.

During periods of heightened volatility linked to the Iran-US war, the government relied more on private placements to secure funding. However, investor sentiment has improved in recent months following economic reforms and greater exchange-rate stability, S&P noted.
For the banking sector, S&P expects issuance to remain concentrated in short-tenor instruments and primarily in the domestic market.

The agency said access to international funding markets is likely to remain limited, with external funding relying mainly on bilateral relationships rather than large-scale international bond issuance.

Egyptian banks continue to have strong local-currency liquidity, which positions them as an important funding source for corporates, particularly larger companies and more resilient sectors. However, elevated funding costs and competition from state-owned borrowers continue to weigh on financing conditions, S&P said.
(Reporting by Ahmad Mousa; editing by Seban Scaria)

title: Egypt targets longer-term debt as it expands sukuk, sustainable financing
